Question ID: ALG1_U01_L03_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

What is 3/4 written as a decimal?

feedback.text: This confuses the numerator and denominator with decimal digits. Divide 3 by 4 to convert the fraction.
Since 3 divided by 4 equals 0.75, 3/4 = 0.75.
This places the numerator and denominator beside each other instead of dividing. A fraction represents division.
This gives the percent value without the percent symbol. As a decimal, the value is 0.75.

Question ID: ALG1_U01_L03_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

What is 0.6 written as a percent?

feedback.text: This moves the decimal only one place. To write a decimal as a percent, multiply by 100.
This keeps the decimal unchanged. Percent means out of 100, so the value must be multiplied by 100.
This moves the decimal one place too far. 0.6 is less than 1, so it is 60%, not 600%.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U01_L03_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

What is 35% written as a decimal?

feedback.text: Percent means out of 100, so 35% = 35/100 = 0.35.
This moves the decimal one place instead of two. Divide the percent by 100 to convert to a decimal.
This keeps the percent number unchanged. A percent must be divided by 100 to become a decimal.
This moves the decimal three places. For percent to decimal, move two places left.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U01_L03_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

What is 25% of 48?

feedback.text: This treats 25% like 50%. Remember that 25% is one-fourth of the whole.
This uses the percent number as the answer instead of finding the percent of 48.
25% = 1/4, and one-fourth of 48 is 12.
This multiplies by 2.5 instead of 0.25. Convert 25% to 0.25 before multiplying.

Question ID: ALG1_U01_L03_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

A student reads 72 pages in 4 hours. What is the unit rate in pages per hour?

feedback.text: This adds the numbers instead of dividing. A unit rate compares to 1 hour.
72 / 4 = 18, so the student reads 18 pages per hour.
This subtracts the numbers instead of dividing. Use pages divided by hours.
This multiplies the numbers. A unit rate requires division by the number of hours.
